key_findings.finding: The directly relevant promoter variant is a short tandem repeat, (TAAA)n, in the PCA3 promoter. The initial Chinese case-control study (PMID 21655300, “Association of short tandem repeat polymorphism in the promoter of prostate cancer antigen 3 gene with the risk of prostate cancer,” PLoS One 2011) sequenced peripheral-blood DNA from 186 prostate-cancer cases and 135 healthy controls; five repeat-length polymorphisms produced eight genotypes, grouped as ≤10, 11, or ≥12 total TAAA repeats. Relative to ≤10 repeats, 11 repeats were associated with higher risk (OR 1.76, 95% CI 1.07–2.89) and ≥12 repeats with markedly higher risk (OR 5.28, 95% CI 1.76–15.89). The abstract reports significant associations by CIs excluding 1, but does not provide exact P values.

source_tools.relevance: Primary study abstract and results preview

key_findings.finding: A later Chinese report (PMID 25975686, “[Association of polymorphism in the promoter region of PCA3 gene with risk of prosate cancer],” Chinese Journal of Oncology 2015) examined 186 prostate-cancer patients, 141 BPH patients, and 135 healthy controls. It again identified the same promoter TAAA repeat-length polymorphism and eight genotypes; versus ≤10 repeats, 11 repeats had OR 1.74 (95% CI 1.06–2.87) and ≥12 repeats had OR 5.63 (95% CI 1.85–17.19), adjusted for sex and age. The abstract also reports an AG/CA mutation in the promoter 18–19 bp region in 62.4% of PCa patients, but gives no comparative control estimate, CI, or P value, so that result cannot independently establish risk association.

Another Chinese study (PMID 25445501, “Long noncoding RNA PCA3 gene promoter region is related to the risk of prostate cancer on Chinese males,” Experimental and Molecular Pathology 2014) included 120 PCa cases and 120 BPH cases, assessed the TAAA repeat in paired blood leukocytes and prostate tissue, and concluded that longer repeats were associated with increased PCa risk. However, the accessible abstract does not report the numerical ORs, CIs, or P values. It additionally observed somatic tissue-versus-blood repeat changes in 18/120 PCa patients with longer tissue repeats and 3/120 with shorter repeats; these are tissue/acquired changes, not germline case-control evidence.

The evidence is not a clean, independently replicated genetic association. The 2014 and 2015 papers appear to follow the same TAAA-promoter finding, and the search identified no additional clearly independent Chinese replication with full effect estimates. A 2017 paper (PMID 29203868) is relevant to a PCA3 promoter microsatellite but was retrieved only as a citation/context result and should not be treated as confirmation of the Chinese association without checking its full population and estimates.

source_tools.relevance: Search for replication and related studies

key_findings.finding: PCA3 overexpression and expression-based biomarker studies are mechanistically or diagnostically related but are not promoter-genotype evidence. The promoter association studies specifically tested inherited repeat length (and, in the 2015 report, an incompletely quantified promoter AG/CA change), whereas expression papers measure PCA3 RNA levels and should not be conflated with these variants.
